title_ar: الشيخ الددو يشارك في مؤتمر "حقوق الإنسان بين الشعارات والحقائق" المنعقد بالخرطوم
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in the Conference "Human Rights: Between Slogans and Realities", Held in Khartoum
body_ar: يشارك الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء اليوم السبت 3 رجب 1433 الموافق 23 يونيو 2012م في مؤتمر "حقوق الإنسان.. بين الشعارات والحقائق" الذي يقام برعاية رئاسة الجمهوريّة السودانيّة وبتنظيم من مجلة البيان والمركز العربي للدراسات وقناة طيبة الفضائيّة. ويستمر المؤتمر الذي يعقد في قاعة الصداقة بالعاصمة السودانية الخرطوم لمدة ثلاثة أيام، حيث تشارك فيه وفود عربيّة وإسلاميّة وشخصيات مؤثرة في الحالة السياسيّة العربيّة. وتشمل محاور المؤتمر عدد من القضايا الإسلاميّة وعلى رأسها القضية الفلسطينيّة وازدواجيّة المعايير التي تتعامل بها المؤسّسات الأممية مع القضايا الإنسانيّة في فلسطين المحتلة ومدينة القدس بشكلٍ خاص، كما تتضمن محاور المؤتمر الوضع الإنساني للشعب السوري الذي يرزح تحت طغيان النظام السوري، وكذلك الشأن العراقي واستباحة أرواح الأبرياء هناك.
body_en:
Today, Saturday 3 Rajab 1433, corresponding to 23 June 2012, Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, is taking part in the conference "Human Rights: Between Slogans and Realities", held under the patronage of the presidency of the Republic of the Sudan and organised by al-Bayan magazine, the Arab Centre for Studies and the Taybah satellite channel.

The conference, which is convened in the Friendship Hall in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, runs for three days, with Arab and Islamic delegations taking part in it, and figures influential in the Arab political situation.

The conference's axes take in a number of Islamic causes, foremost among them the Palestinian cause and the double standards with which the international institutions deal with humanitarian questions in occupied Palestine and in the city of Jerusalem in particular. The conference's axes also comprise the humanitarian situation of the Syrian people, who groan under the tyranny of the Syrian regime, and likewise the Iraqi affair and the treating of the lives of the innocent there as forfeit.

flags.arabic: الشعب السوري الذي يرزح تحت طغيان النظام السوري ... استباحة أرواح الأبرياء ... برعاية رئاسة الجمهوريّة السودانيّة
flags.context: the conference's announced agenda and its patron
options: translate faithfully and refer the publication decision upward
translate and publish as ordinary content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12. Three charged elements sit in one short record: the conference is held under the patronage of the Sudanese presidency, which in June 2012 meant a head of state under ICC indictment; its agenda names the Syrian regime's tyranny and the violation of innocent life in Iraq; and it frames the international human-rights institutions as applying double standards over Palestine. None of this is the Sheikh's own wording — every sentence describes the conference, and the record contains not one word he said there. That distinction is the whole editorial question: an English page under his name listing this agenda will be read as his platform. Nothing has been softened; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: وكذلك الشأن العراقي واستباحة أرواح الأبرياء هناك
options: the treating of the lives of the innocent as forfeit
the declaring of innocent blood to be lawful
flags.note: HOMONYM WARNING, and a dangerous one. istibāḥah shares a root with mubāḥ, which the glossary fixes as 'permissible' — one of the five rulings. Read through that entry the phrase would come out as 'the permissibility of the lives of the innocent', which inverts the sense: istibāḥah is treating as fair game what is in fact inviolable, and the phrase is an accusation, not a ruling. The glossary rendering has deliberately not been used, and no ruling word appears in the English.

flags.context: ازدواجيّة المعايير التي تتعامل بها المؤسّسات الأممية
options: the institutions of the community of nations
flags.note: أممي is ambiguous between 'international' in general and 'pertaining to the United Nations' (الأمم المتحدة) in particular. In a sentence about double standards over Palestine, UN bodies are plainly the target, but the Arabic does not say so and 'international institutions' keeps the same breadth. Note that the word also has a third life as the adjective from ummah; that sense is not in play here.

flags.context: وتشمل محاور المؤتمر عدد من القضايا
flags.note: miḥwar, literally an axle, is the standard Arabic word for a conference strand or theme. 'Axes' is used across this slice for consistency with records 791 and elsewhere, though 'themes' reads more naturally in English; a reviewer should fix one across the corpus. Note the source's grammatical slip: عدد should be عددا after تشمل.

translator_notes: A news-desk announcement written on the conference's opening day. It records the Sheikh's participation and carries none of his words.
The CMS timestamp, 23 June 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body dates the opening to Saturday 3 Rajab 1433 / 23 June 2012.
The source writes the feminine ending with a shadda in several words (الجمهوريّة, الإسلاميّة) and not in others; this is ordinary typing variation and has been left as served.
